<div align="left" data-conditional="_gpt2lcv4_tim2cc"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="113.59px"/><col width="496.24px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:25</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 24</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SMSPE:</span> SMS preload enable</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">This bit selects whether the SMS[3:0] bitfield is preloaded.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0: SMS[3:0] bitfield is not preloaded</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1: SMS[3:0] preload is enabled</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 23:22</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 19:17</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="85.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">MSM:</span><span style="font-style:Italic;"> </span>Master/slave mode</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   No action</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   The effect of an event on the trigger input (tim_trgi) is delayed to allow a perfect synchronization between the current timer and its slaves (through tim_trgo). It is useful if the user wants to synchronize several timers on a single external event.</p></td></tr><tr height="422.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 21, 20, 6, 5, 4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TS[4:0]:</span> Trigger selection</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield selects the trigger input to be used to synchronize the counter.</p><p class="TableIndent">00000:   Internal Trigger 0 (tim_itr0)</p><p class="TableIndent">00001:   Internal Trigger 1 (tim_itr1)</p><p class="TableIndent">00010:   Internal Trigger 2 (tim_itr2)</p><p class="TableIndent">00011:   Internal Trigger 3 (tim_itr3)</p><p class="TableIndent">00100:   tim_ti1 Edge Detector (tim_ti1f_ed)</p><p class="TableIndent">00101:   Filtered Timer Input 1 (tim_ti1fp1)</p><p class="TableIndent">00110:   Filtered Timer Input 2 (tim_ti2fp2)</p><p class="TableIndent">00111:   Reserved</p><p class="TableIndent">01000:   Internal Trigger 4 (tim_itr4)</p><p class="TableIndent">01001:   Internal Trigger 5 (tim_itr5)</p><p class="TableIndent">01010:   Internal Trigger 6 (tim_itr6)</p><p class="TableIndent">01011:   Internal Trigger 7 (tim_itr7)</p><p class="TableIndent">01100:   Internal Trigger 8 (tim_itr8)</p><p class="TableIndent">01101:   Internal Trigger 9 (tim_itr9)</p><p class="TableIndent">01110:   Internal Trigger 10 (tim_itr10)</p><p class="TableIndent">10000: Internal trigger 12 (tim_itr12)</p><p class="TableIndent">10001: Internal trigger 13 (tim_itr13)</p><p class="TableIndent">10010: Internal trigger 14 (tim_itr14)</p><p class="TableIndent">10011: Internal trigger 15 (tim_itr15)</p><p class="TableIndent">Others: Reserved</p><p class="TableIndent">See <span class="CrossRef" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;"><a href="#XREF_92892__29_4_2_TIM1/TIM8/TIM20_pins_and_internal_signals22" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 31.4.2: TIM15/TIM16/TIM17 pins and internal signals</a></span> for more details on tim_itrx meaning for each timer.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>These bits must be changed only when they are not used (for example when SMS = 000) to avoid wrong edge detections at the transition.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="485.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 16, 2, 1, 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SMS[3:0]:</span> Slave mode selection</p><p class="TableIndent">When external signals are selected the active edge of the trigger signal (tim_trgi) is linked to the polarity selected on the external input (refer to ETP bit in TIMx_SMCR for tim_etr_in and CCxP/CCxNP bits in TIMx_CCER register for tim_ti1fp1 and tim_ti2fp2).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0000:   Slave mode disabled - if CEN = 1 then the prescaler is clocked directly by the internal clock.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0001: Reserved</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0010:   Reserved</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0011:   Reserved</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0100:   Reset mode - Rising edge of the selected trigger input (tim_trgi) reinitializes the counter and generates an update of the registers.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0101:   Gated mode - The counter clock is enabled when the trigger input (tim_trgi) is high. The counter stops (but is not reset) as soon as the trigger becomes low. Both start and stop of the counter are controlled.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0110:   Trigger mode - The counter starts at a rising edge of the trigger tim_trgi (but it is not reset). Only the start of the counter is controlled.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0111:   External Clock mode 1 - Rising edges of the selected trigger (tim_trgi) clock the counter.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1000:   Combined reset + trigger mode - Rising edge of the selected trigger input (tim_trgi) reinitializes the counter, generates an update of the registers and starts the counter.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1001:   Combined gated + reset mode - The counter clock is enabled when the trigger input (tim_trgi) is high. The counter stops and is reset) as soon as the trigger becomes low. Both start and stop of the counter are controlled.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">Others: Reserved.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The gated mode must not be used if tim_ti1f_ed is selected as the trigger input (TS = 00100). Indeed, tim_ti1f_ed outputs 1 pulse for each transition on tim_ti1f, whereas the gated mode checks the level of the trigger signal.</p><p class="RegTNote_">The clock of the slave peripherals (such as timer and ADC) receiving the tim_trgo signal must be enabled prior to receive events from the master timer, and the clock frequency (prescaler) must not be changed on-the-fly while triggers are received from the master timer.</p></td></tr></table></div>

Reset value: 0x0000

<div align="left" data-conditional="_gpt2lcv4_tim2cc"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="114.50px"/><col width="495.27px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:11</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC2OF</span>: Capture/Compare 2 overcapture flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to CC1OF description</p></td></tr><tr height="101.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 9</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC1OF</span>: Capture/Compare 1 overcapture flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This flag is set by hardware only when the corresponding channel is configured in input capture mode. It is cleared by software by writing it to 0.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   No overcapture has been detected</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1: The counter value has been captured in TIM15_CCR1 register while CC1IF flag was already set</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="85.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BIF</span>: Break interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This flag is set by hardware as soon as the break input goes active. It can be cleared by software if the break input is not active.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No break event occurred<br/>1: An active level has been detected on the break input</p></td></tr><tr height="114.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 6</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TIF</span>: Trigger interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This flag is set by hardware on the TRG trigger event (active edge detected on tim_trgi input when the slave mode controller is enabled in all modes but gated mode, both edges in case gated mode is selected). It is set when the counter starts or stops when gated mode is selected. It is cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No trigger event occurred<br/>1: Trigger interrupt pending</p></td></tr><tr height="85.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="Bold" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:Bold;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">COMIF:</span> COM interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This flag is set by hardware on a COM event (once the capture/compare control bits –CCxE, CCxNE, OCxM– have been updated). It is cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No COM event occurred<br/>1: COM interrupt pending</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 4:3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC2IF</span>: Capture/Compare 2 interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">refer to CC1IF description</p></td></tr><tr height="221.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC1IF</span>: Capture/Compare 1 interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This flag is set by hardware. It is cleared by software (input capture or output compare mode) or by reading the TIMx_CCR1 register (input capture mode only).</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No compare match / No input capture occurred</p><p class="TableIndent">1: A compare match or an input capture occurred</p><p class="TableIndent"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC1 is configured as output</span>: this flag is set when the content of the counter TIMx_CNT matches the content of the TIMx_CCR1 register. When the content of TIMx_CCR1 is greater than the content of TIMx_ARR, the CC1IF bit goes high on the counter overflow (in up-counting and up/down-counting modes) or underflow (in downcounting mode). There are 3 possible options for flag setting in center-aligned mode, refer to the CMS bits in the TIMx_CR1 register for the full description.</p><p class="TableIndent"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC1 is configured as input</span>: this bit is set when counter value has been captured in TIMx_CCR1 register (an edge has been detected on IC1, as per the edge sensitivity defined with the CC1P and CC1NP bits setting, in TIMx_CCER).</p></td></tr><tr height="166.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">UIF</span>: Update interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware on an update event. It is cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No update occurred.<br/>1: Update interrupt pending. This bit is set by hardware when the registers are updated:</p><p class="TableBullet" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;text-indent : -8.50pt;">–<span style="padding-right:4pt ;">​</span>At overflow regarding the repetition counter value (update if repetition counter = 0) and if the UDIS = 0 in the TIM15_CR1 register.</p><p class="TableBullet" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;text-indent : -8.50pt;">–<span style="padding-right:4pt ;">​</span>When CNT is reinitialized by software using the UG bit in TIM15_EGR register, if URS = 0 and UDIS = 0 in the TIM15_CR1 register.</p><p class="TableBullet" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;text-indent : -8.50pt;">–<span style="padding-right:4pt ;">​</span>When CNT is reinitialized by a trigger event (refer to <span class="CrossRef" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;"><a href="#XREF_75067__12_5_3_Slave_mode_control_register_(TIM1_SMCR)22" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 31.7.3: TIM15 slave mode control register (TIM15_SMCR)</a></span>), if URS = 0 and UDIS = 0 in the TIM15_CR1 register.</p></td></tr></table></div>

Reset value: 0x0000

<div align="left" data-conditional="_gpt2lcv4_tim2cc"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="113.79px"/><col width="497.21px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="101.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BG</span>: Break generation</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by software in order to generate an event, it is automatically cleared by hardware.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   No action</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   A break event is generated. MOE bit is cleared and BIF flag is set. Related interrupt or DMA transfer can occur if enabled.</p></td></tr><tr height="101.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 6</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TG</span>: Trigger generation</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by software in order to generate an event, it is automatically cleared by hardware.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   No action</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   The TIF flag is set in TIM15_SR register. Related interrupt or DMA transfer can occur if enabled</p></td></tr><tr height="88.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="Bold" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:Bold;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">COMG:</span> Capture/Compare control update generation</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit can be set by software, it is automatically cleared by hardware.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No action<br/>1: When the CCPC bit is set, it is possible to update the CCxE, CCxNE and OCxM bits</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit acts only on channels that have a complementary output.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 4:3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC2G</span>: Capture/Compare 2 generation</p><p class="TableBodyL">Refer to CC1G description</p></td></tr><tr height="174.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC1G</span>: Capture/Compare 1 generation</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by software in order to generate an event, it is automatically cleared by hardware.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   No action</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1    A capture/compare event is generated on channel 1:<br/><span style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC1 is configured as output:<br/></span>CC1IF flag is set, Corresponding interrupt or DMA request is sent if enabled.<br/><span style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC1 is configured as input:<br/></span>The current value of the counter is captured in TIM15_CCR1 register. The CC1IF flag is set, the corresponding interrupt or DMA request is sent if enabled. The CC1OF flag is set if the CC1IF flag was already high.</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">UG</span>: Update generation</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit can be set by software, it is automatically cleared by hardware.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   No action</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   Reinitialize the counter and generates an update of the registers. Note that the prescaler counter is cleared too (anyway the prescaler ratio is not affected).</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 31.7.7 TIM15 capture/compare mode register 1 (TIM15\_CCMR1)

Address offset: 0x18

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

The same register can be used for input capture mode (this section) or for output compare mode (next section). The direction of a channel is defined by configuring the corresponding CCxS bits. All the other bits of this register have a different function for input capture and for output compare modes. It is possible to combine both modes independently (for example channel 1 in input capture mode and channel 2 in output compare mode).

Input capture mode

  


<div align="left" data-conditional="_gpt2lcv4_tim2cc"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="70.59px"/><col width="542.67px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:12</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IC2F[3:0]</span>:<span style="font-weight:Bold;"> </span>Input capture 2 filter</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 11:10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IC2PSC[1:0]</span>: Input capture 2 prescaler</p></td></tr><tr height="132.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 9:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC2S[1:0]</span>: Capture/Compare 2 selection</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the direction of the channel (input/output) as well as the used input. </p><p class="TableIndent">00: CC2 channel is configured as output<br/>01: CC2 channel is configured as input, tim_ic2 is mapped on tim_ti2<br/>10: CC2 channel is configured as input, tim_ic2 is mapped on tim_ti1<br/>11: CC2 channel is configured as input, tim_ic2 is mapped on tim_trc. This mode is working only if an internal trigger input is selected through TS bit (TIM15_SMCR register)</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>CC2S bits are writable only when the channel is OFF (CC2E = 0 in TIM15_CCER).</p></td></tr><tr height="325.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 7:4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IC1F[3:0]</span>:<span style="font-weight:Bold;"> </span>Input capture 1 filter</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the frequency used to sample tim_ti1 input and the length of the digital filter applied to tim_ti1. The digital filter is made of an event counter in which N consecutive events are needed to validate a transition on the output:</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0000: No filter, sampling is done at f<sub>DTS</sub></p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0001:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>tim_ker_ck</sub>, N = 2</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0010:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>tim_ker_ck</sub>, N = 4</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0011:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; The prescaler is reset as soon as CC1E = 0 (TIM15_CCER register).</p><p class="TableIndent">00: no prescaler, capture is done each time an edge is detected on the capture input<br/>01: capture is done once every 2 events<br/>10: capture is done once every 4 events<br/>11: capture is done once every 8 events</p></td></tr><tr height="132.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 1:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC1S[1:0]</span>: Capture/Compare 1 selection</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the direction of the channel (input/output) as well as the used input. </p><p class="TableIndent">00: CC1 channel is configured as output<br/>01: CC1 channel is configured as input, tim_ic1 is mapped on tim_ti1<br/>10: CC1 channel is configured as input, tim_ic1 is mapped on tim_ti2<br/>11: CC1 channel is configured as input, tim_ic1 is mapped on tim_trc. This mode is working only if an internal trigger input is selected through TS bit (TIM15_SMCR register)</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>CC1S bits are writable only when the channel is OFF (CC1E = 0 in TIM15_CCER).</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 31.7.8 TIM15 capture/compare mode register 1 [alternate]   (  
TIM15\_CCMR1)

Address offset: 0x18

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

The same register can be used for output compare mode (this section) or for input capture mode (previous section). The direction of a channel is defined by configuring the corresponding CCxS bits. All the other bits of this register have a different function for input capture and for output compare modes. It is possible to combine both modes independently (for example channel 1 in input capture mode and channel 2 in output compare mode).

Output compare mode:


<div align="left" data-conditional="_gpt2lcv4_tim2cc"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.41px"/><col width="495.21px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:25</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 23:17</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 15</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC2CE</span>: Output compare 2 clear enable</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 24, 14:12</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC2M[3:0]</span>: Output compare 2 mode</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 11</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC2PE</span>: Output compare 2 preload enable</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC2FE</span>: Output compare 2 fast enable</p></td></tr><tr height="136.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 9:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC2S[1:0]</span>: Capture/Compare 2 selection</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the direction of the channel (input/output) as well as the used input.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">00:   CC2 channel is configured as output.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">01:   CC2 channel is configured as input, tim_ic2 is mapped on tim_ti2.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">10:    C2 channel is configured as input, tim_ic2 is mapped on tim_ti1.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">11:   CC2 channel is configured as input, tim_ic2 is mapped on tim_trc. This mode is working only if an internal trigger input is selected through the TS bit (TIM15_SMCR register)</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>CC2S bits are writable only when the channel is OFF (CC2E = 0 in TIM15_CCER).</p></td></tr><tr height="54.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC1CE</span>: Output compare 1 clear enable</p><p class="TableIndent">0: tim_oc1ref is not affected by the tim_ocref_clr_int input.<br/>1: tim_oc1ref is cleared as soon as a High level is detected on tim_ocref_clr_int input.</p></td></tr><tr height="758.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 16, 6:4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC1M[3:0]</span>: Output compare 1 mode</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits define the behavior of the output reference signal tim_oc1ref from which tim_oc1 and tim_oc1n are derived. tim_oc1ref is active high whereas tim_oc1 and tim_oc1n active level depends on CC1P and CC1NP bits.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0000:   Frozen - The comparison between the output compare register TIM15_CCR1 and the counter TIM15_CNT has no effect on the outputs. This mode can be used when the timer serves as a software timebase. When the frozen mode is enabled during timer operation, the output keeps the state (active or inactive) it had before entering the frozen state.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0001:   Set channel 1 to active level on match. tim_oc1ref signal is forced high when the counter TIM15_CNT matches the capture/compare register 1 (TIM15_CCR1).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0010:   Set channel 1 to inactive level on match. tim_oc1ref signal is forced low when the counter TIM15_CNT matches the capture/compare register 1 (TIM15_CCR1).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0011:   Toggle - tim_oc1ref toggles when TIM15_CNT = TIM15_CCR1.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0100:   Force inactive level - tim_oc1ref is forced low.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0101:   Force active level - tim_oc1ref is forced high.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0110:   PWM mode 1 - Channel 1 is active as long as TIM15_CNT&lt;TIM15_CCR1 else inactive. </p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0111:   PWM mode 2 - Channel 1 is inactive as long as TIM15_CNT&lt;TIM15_CCR1 else active.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1000:   Retrigerrable<span style="font-size : 10.00pt;"> </span>OPM mode 1 - In up-counting mode, the channel is active until a trigger event is detected (on tim_trgi signal). Then, a comparison is performed as in PWM mode 1 and the channels becomes active again at the next update. In down-counting mode, the channel is inactive until a trigger event is detected (on tim_trgi signal). Then, a comparison is performed as in PWM mode 1 and the channels becomes inactive again at the next update.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1001:   Retrigerrable<span style="font-size : 10.00pt;"> </span>OPM mode 2 - In up-counting mode, the channel is inactive until a trigger event is detected (on tim_trgi signal). Then, a comparison is performed as in PWM mode 2 and the channels becomes inactive again at the next update. In down-counting mode, the channel is active until a trigger event is detected (on tim_trgi signal). Then, a comparison is performed as in PWM mode 1 and the channels becomes active again at the next update.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1010:   Reserved</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1011:   Reserved</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1100:   Combined PWM mode 1 - tim_oc1ref has the same behavior as in PWM mode 1. tim_oc1refc is the logical OR between tim_oc1ref and tim_oc2ref.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1101:   Combined PWM mode 2 - tim_oc1ref has the same behavior as in PWM mode 2. tim_oc1refc is the logical AND between tim_oc1ref and tim_oc2ref.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1110:   Reserved,</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1111:   Reserved,</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>These bits can not be modified as long as LOCK level 3 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIM15_BDTR register) and CC1S = 00 (the channel is configured in output).</p><p class="RegTNote_">In PWM mode, the OCREF level changes when the result of the comparison changes, when the output compare mode switches from “frozen” mode to “PWM” mode and when the output compare mode switches from “force active/inactive” mode to “PWM” mode.</p><p class="RegTNote_">On channels that have a complementary output, this bitfield is preloaded. If the CCPC bit is set in the TIM15_CR2 register then the OC1M active bits take the new value from the preloaded bits only when a COM event is generated.</p></td></tr><tr height="117.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC1PE</span>: Output Compare 1 preload enable</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   Preload register on TIM15_CCR1 disabled. TIM15_CCR1 can be written at anytime, the new value is taken in account immediately.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   Preload register on TIM15_CCR1 enabled. Read/Write operations access the preload register. TIM15_CCR1 preload value is loaded in the active register at each update event.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>These bits can not be modified as long as LOCK level 3 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIM15_BDTR register) and CC1S = 00 (the channel is configured in output).</p></td></tr><tr height="174.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC1FE</span>: Output Compare 1 fast enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit decreases the latency between a trigger event and a transition on the timer output. It must be used in one-pulse mode (OPM bit set in TIMx_CR1 register), to have the output pulse starting as soon as possible after the starting trigger.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   CC1 behaves normally depending on counter and CCR1 values even when the trigger is ON. The minimum delay to activate CC1 output when an edge occurs on the trigger input is 5 clock cycles.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   An active edge on the trigger input acts like a compare match on CC1 output. Then, tim_ocx is set to the compare level independently of the result of the comparison. Delay to sample the trigger input and to activate CC1 output is reduced to 3 clock cycles. OCFE acts only if the channel is configured in PWM1 or PWM2 mode.</p></td></tr><tr height="132.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 1:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC1S[1:0]</span>: Capture/Compare 1 selection</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the direction of the channel (input/output) as well as the used input. </p><p class="TableIndent">00: CC1 channel is configured as output.<br/>01: CC1 channel is configured as input, tim_ic1 is mapped on tim_ti1.<br/>10: CC1 channel is configured as input, tim_ic1 is mapped on tim_ti2.<br/>11: CC1 channel is configured as input, tim_ic1 is mapped on tim_trc. This mode is working only if an internal trigger input is selected through TS bit (TIM15_SMCR register)</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>CC1S bits are writable only when the channel is OFF (CC1E = 0 in TIM15_CCER).</p></td></tr></table></div>

Address offset: 0x20

Reset value: 0x0000

<div align="left" data-conditional="_gpt2lcv4_tim2cc"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.50px"/><col width="496.90px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC2NP</span>: Capture/Compare 2 complementary output polarity</p><p class="TableBodyL">Refer to CC1NP description</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 6</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC2P</span>: Capture/Compare 2 output polarity</p><p class="TableBodyL">Refer to CC1P description</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC2E</span>: Capture/Compare 2 output enable</p><p class="TableBodyL">Refer to CC1E description</p></td></tr><tr height="196.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC1NP</span>: Capture/Compare 1 complementary output polarity</p><p class="TableIndent">CC1 channel configured as output:</p><p class="TableIndent">0: tim_oc1n active high<br/>1: tim_oc1n active low</p><p class="TableIndent">CC1 channel configured as input:</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is used in conjunction with CC1P to define the polarity of tim_ti1fp1 and tim_ti2fp1. Refer to CC1P description.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit is not writable as soon as LOCK level 2 or 3 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIM15_BDTR register) and CC1S = 00 (the channel is configured in output).</p><p class="RegTNote_">On channels that have a complementary output, this bit is preloaded. If the CCPC bit is set in the TIM15_CR2 register then the CC1NP active bit takes the new value from the preloaded bit only when a Commutation event is generated.</p></td></tr><tr height="85.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC1NE</span>: Capture/Compare 1 complementary output enable</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   Off - tim_oc1n is not active. tim_oc1n level is then function of MOE, OSSI, OSSR, OIS1, OIS1N and CC1E bits.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   On - tim_oc1n signal is output on the corresponding output pin depending on MOE, OSSI, OSSR, OIS1, OIS1N and CC1E bits.</p></td></tr><tr height="348.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC1P</span>: Capture/Compare 1 output polarity</p><p class="TableIndent">CC1 channel configured as output:</p><p class="TableIndent">0: OC1 active high (output mode) / Edge sensitivity selection (input mode, see below)</p><p class="TableIndent">1: OC1 active low (output mode) / Edge sensitivity selection (input mode, see below)</p><p class="TableIndent"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">When CC1 channel is configured as input</span>, both CC1NP/CC1P bits select the active polarity of TI1FP1 and TI2FP1 for trigger or capture operations.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 104.88pt;">CC1NP = 0, CC1P = 0:   non-inverted/rising edge. The circuit is sensitive to TIxFP1 rising edge (capture or trigger operations in reset, external clock or trigger mode), TIxFP1 is not inverted (trigger operation in gated mode).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 104.88pt;">CC1NP = 0, CC1P = 1:   inverted/falling edge. The circuit is sensitive to TIxFP1 falling edge (capture or trigger operations in reset, external clock or trigger mode), TIxFP1 is inverted (trigger operation in gated mode).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 104.88pt;">CC1NP = 1, CC1P = 1:   non-inverted/both edges/ The circuit is sensitive to both TIxFP1 rising and falling edges (capture or trigger operations in reset, external clock or trigger mode), TIxFP1is not inverted (trigger operation in gated mode).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 104.88pt;">CC1NP = 1, CC1P = 0:   this configuration is reserved, it must not be used.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit is not writable as soon as LOCK level 2 or 3 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIM15_BDTR register).</p><p class="RegTNote_">On channels that have a complementary output, this bit is preloaded. If the CCPC bit is set in the TIM15_CR2 register then the CC1P active bit takes the new value from the preloaded bit only when a Commutation event is generated.</p></td></tr><tr height="101.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC1E</span>: Capture/Compare 1 output enable</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Capture mode disabled / OC1 is not active (see below)</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Capture mode enabled / OC1 signal is output on the corresponding output pin</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">When CC1 channel is configured as output</span>, the OC1 level depends on MOE, OSSI, OSSR, OIS1, OIS1N and CC1NE bits, regardless of the CC1E bits state. Refer to <span class="CrossRef" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;"><a href="#XREF_94940__Table_2__Output_Control_bits_for_complementary_OCx_and_OCxN_Channels_with22" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Table 316</a></span> for details.</p></td></tr></table></div>

The ARR[19:16] bits are reset.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Dithering mode (DITHEN = 1)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the integer part in ARR[19:4]. The ARR[3:0] bitfield contains the dithered part.</p></td></tr></table></div>

<div align="left" data-conditional="_gpt2lcv4_tim2cc"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.14px"/><col width="496.84px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="194.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 7:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">REP[7:0]</span>: Repetition counter reload value</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the update rate of the compare registers (i.e. periodic transfers from preload to active registers) when preload registers are enable. It also defines the update interrupt generation rate, if this interrupt is enable.</p><p class="TableIndent">When the repetition down-counter reaches zero, an update event is generated and it restarts counting from REP value. As the reptition counter is reloaded with REP value only at the repetition update event UEV, any write to the TIM15_RCR register is not taken in account until the next repetition update event.</p><p class="TableIndent">It means in PWM mode (REP+1) corresponds to the number of PWM periods in edge-aligned mode:</p><p class="RegTBullet2">–<span style="padding-right:16pt ;">​</span>The number of PWM periods in edge-aligned mode.</p><p class="RegTBullet2">–<span style="padding-right:16pt ;">​</span>The number of half PWM period in center-aligned mode.</p></td></tr></table></div>

<div align="left" data-conditional="_gpt2lcv4_tim2cc"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.14px"/><col width="495.93px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:20</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="320.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 19:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CCR1[19:0]</span>: Capture/compare 1 value</p><p class="TableIndent"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC1 is configured as output</span>:</p><p class="TableIndent">CCR1 is the value to be loaded in the actual capture/compare 1 register (preload value).</p><p class="TableIndent">It is loaded permanently if the preload feature is not selected in the TIM15_CCMR1 register (bit OC1PE). Else the preload value is copied in the active capture/compare 1 register when an update event occurs.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;"><span style="text-decoration:none;">The active capture/compare register contains the value to be compared to the counter TIM15_CNT and signaled on tim_oc1 output.<br/></span>Non-dithering mode (DITHEN = 0)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the compare value in CCR1[15:0]. The CCR1[19:16] bits are reset.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Dithering mode (DITHEN = 1)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the integer part in CCR1[19:4]. The CCR1[3:0] bitfield contains the dithered part.</p><p class="TableIndent"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC1 is configured as input</span>:</p><p class="TableIndent">CR1 is the counter value transferred by the last input capture 1 event (tim_ic1). The TIMx_CCR1 register is read-only and cannot be programmed.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Non-dithering mode (DITHEN = 0)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the capture value in CCR1[15:0]. The CCR1[19:16] bits are reset.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Dithering mode (DITHEN = 1)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the capture in CCR1[19:4]. The CCR1[3:0] bits are reset.</p></td></tr></table></div>

<div align="left" data-conditional="_gpt2lcv4_tim2cc"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.14px"/><col width="496.84px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:20</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="320.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 19:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CCR2[19:0]</span>: Capture/compare 2 value</p><p class="TableIndent"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC2 is configured as output</span>:</p><p class="TableIndent">CCR2 is the value to be loaded in the actual capture/compare 2 register (preload value).</p><p class="TableIndent">It is loaded permanently if the preload feature is not selected in the TIM15_CCMR2 register (bit OC2PE). Else the preload value is copied in the active capture/compare 2 register when an update event occurs.</p><p class="TableIndent">The active capture/compare register contains the value to be compared to the counter TIM15_CNT and signalled on tim_oc2 output.<br/><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Non-dithering mode (DITHEN = 0)</span></p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the compare value in CCR2[15:0]. The CCR2[19:16] bits are reset.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Dithering mode (DITHEN = 1)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the integer part in CCR2[19:4]. The CCR2[3:0] bitfield contains the dithered part.</p><p class="TableIndent"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC2 is configured as input</span>:</p><p class="TableIndent">CCR2 is the counter value transferred by the last input capture 1 event (tim_ic2). The TIMx_CCR2 register is read-only and cannot be programmed.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Non-dithering mode (DITHEN = 0)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the capture value in CCR2[15:0]. The CCR2[19:16] bits are reset.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Dithering mode (DITHEN = 1)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the capture in CCR2[19:4]. The CCR2[3:0] bits are reset.</p></td></tr></table></div>

**Note:**

As the BKBID, BKDSRM, BKF[3:0], AOE, BKP, BKE, OSSI, OSSR, and DTG[7:0] bits may be write-locked depending on the LOCK configuration, it may be necessary to configure all of them during the first write access to the TIM15\_BDTR register.


<div align="left" data-conditional="_gpt2lcv4_tim2cc"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="113.54px"/><col width="500.63px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:29</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="149.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 28</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BKBID</span>: Break bidirectional</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Break input tim_brk in input mode<br/>1: Break input tim_brk in bidirectional mode</p><p class="TableIndent">In the bidirectional mode (BKBID bit set to 1), the break input is configured both in input mode and in open drain output mode. Any active break event asserts a low logic level on the Break input to indicate an internal break event to external devices.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit cannot be modified as long as LOCK level 1 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIM15_BDTR register).</p><p class="RegTNote_">Any write operation to this bit takes a delay of 1 APB clock cycle to become effective.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 27</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="133.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 26</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BKDSRM</span>: Break disarm</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Break input tim_brk is armed<br/>1: Break input tim_brk is disarmed</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is cleared by hardware when no break source is active.</p><p class="TableIndent">The BKDSRM bit must be set by software to release the bidirectional output control (open-drain output in Hi-Z state) and then be polled until it is reset by hardware, indicating that the fault condition has disappeared.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>Any write operation to this bit takes a delay of 1 APB clock cycle to become effective.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 25:20</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="357.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 19:16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BKF[3:0]</span>:<span style="font-weight:Bold;"> </span>Break filter</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the frequency used to sample the tim_brk input signal and the length of the digital filter applied to tim_brk. The digital filter is made of an event counter in which N events are needed to validate a transition on the output:</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0000: No filter, tim_brk acts asynchronously</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0001:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>tim_ker_ck</sub>, N = 2</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0010:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>tim_ker_ck</sub>, N = 4</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0011:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>tim_ker_ck</sub>, N = 8</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0100:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/2, N = 6</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0101:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/2, N = 8</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0110:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/4, N = 6</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0111:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/4, N = 8</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1000:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/8, N = 6</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1001:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/8, N = 8</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1010:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/16, N = 5</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1011:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/16, N = 6</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1100:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/16, N = 8</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1101:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/32, N = 5</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1110:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/32, N = 6</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1111:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/32, N = 8</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit cannot be modified when LOCK level 1 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIM15_BDTR register).</p></td></tr><tr height="161.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 15</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">MOE</span>: Main output enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is cleared asynchronously by hardware as soon as the tim_brk input is active. It is set by software or automatically depending on the AOE bit. It is acting only on the channels which are configured in output.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   tim_ocx and tim_ocxn outputs are disabled or forced to idle state depending on the OSSI bit.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   tim_ocx and tim_ocxn outputs are enabled if their respective enable bits are set (CCxE, CCxNE in TIM15_CCER register)</p><p class="TableIndent">See tim_ocx/tim_ocxn enable description for more details (<span class="CrossRef" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;"><a href="#XREF_67448__1_5_10_Capture/Compare_Enable_Register_(GPT_CCER)22" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 31.7.9: TIM15 capture/compare enable register (TIM15_CCER) on page 1466</a></span>).</p></td></tr><tr height="102.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 14</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">AOE</span>: Automatic output enable</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   MOE can be set only by software</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   MOE can be set by software or automatically at the next update event (if the break input is not be active)</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit can not be modified as long as LOCK level 1 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIM15_BDTR register).</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 13</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BKP</span>: Break polarity</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Break input tim_brk is active low<br/>1: Break input tim_brk is active high</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit can not be modified as long as LOCK level 1 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIM15_BDTR register).</p><p class="RegTNote_">Any write operation to this bit takes a delay of 1 APB clock cycle to become effective.</p></td></tr><tr height="102.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 12</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BKE</span>: Break enable</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Break inputs (tim_brk and tim_sys_brk clock failure event) disabled<br/>1; Break inputs (tim_brk and tim_sys_brk clock failure event) enabled</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit cannot be modified when LOCK level 1 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIM15_BDTR register).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>Any write operation to this bit takes a delay of 1 APB clock cycle to become effective.</p></td></tr><tr height="193.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 11</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OSSR</span>:<span style="font-weight:Bold;"> </span>Off-state selection for Run mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is used when MOE = 1 on channels that have a complementary output which are configured as outputs. OSSR is not implemented if no complementary output is implemented in the timer.</p><p class="TableIndent">See tim_ocx/tim_ocxn enable description for more details (<span class="CrossRef" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;"><a href="#XREF_67448__1_5_10_Capture/Compare_Enable_Register_(GPT_CCER)22" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 31.7.9: TIM15 capture/compare enable register (TIM15_CCER) on page 1466</a></span>).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   When inactive, tim_ocx/tim_ocxn outputs are disabled (the timer releases the output control which is taken over by the GPIO, which forces a Hi-Z state)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   When inactive, tim_ocx/tim_ocxn outputs are enabled with their inactive level as soon as CCxE = 1 or CCxNE = 1 (the output is still controlled by the timer). </p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit can not be modified as soon as the LOCK level 2 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIM15_BDTR register).</p></td></tr><tr height="162.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OSSI</span>:<span style="font-weight:Bold;"> </span>Off-state selection for Idle mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is used when MOE = 0 on channels configured as outputs.<br/>See tim_ocx/tim_ocxn enable description for more details (<span class="CrossRef" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;"><a href="#XREF_67448__1_5_10_Capture/Compare_Enable_Register_(GPT_CCER)22" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 31.7.9: TIM15 capture/compare enable register (TIM15_CCER) on page 1466</a></span>).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   When inactive, tim_ocx/tim_ocxn outputs are disabled (tim_ocx/tim_ocxn enable output signal = 0)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   When inactive, tim_ocx/tim_ocxn outputs are forced first with their idle level as soon as CCxE = 1 or CCxNE = 1. tim_ocx/tim_ocxn enable output signal = 1)</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit can not be modified as soon as the LOCK level 2 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIM15_BDTR register).</p></td></tr><tr height="224.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 9:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">LOCK[1:0]</span>: Lock configuration</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits offer a write protection against software errors.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">00:   LOCK OFF - No bit is write protected</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">01:   LOCK Level 1 = DTG bits in TIM15_BDTR register, OISx and OISxN bits in TIM15_CR2 register and BKBID/BKE/BKP/AOE bits in TIM15_BDTR register can no longer be written</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">10:   LOCK Level 2 = LOCK Level 1 + CC Polarity bits (CCxP/CCxNP bits in TIM15_CCER register, as long as the related channel is configured in output through the CCxS bits) as well as OSSR and OSSI bits can no longer be written.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">11:    OCK Level 3 = LOCK Level 2 + CC Control bits (OCxM and OCxPE bits in TIM15_CCMRx registers, as long as the related channel is configured in output through the CCxS bits) can no longer be written.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The LOCK bits can be written only once after the reset. Once the TIM15_BDTR register has been written, their content is frozen until the next reset.</p></td></tr><tr height="220.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 7:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DTG[7:0]</span>: Dead-time generator setup</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the duration of the dead-time inserted between the complementary outputs. DT correspond to this duration.</p><p class="TableIndent">DTG[7:5] = 0xx  → DT = DTG[7:0]x t<sub>dtg</sub> with t<sub>dtg</sub> = t<sub>DTS<br/></sub>DTG[7:5] = 10x → DT = (64+DTG[5:0])xt<sub>dtg</sub> with T<sub>dtg</sub> = 2xt<sub>DTS<br/></sub>DTG[7:5] = 110 → DT = (32+DTG[4:0])xt<sub>dtg</sub> with T<sub>dtg</sub> = 8xt<sub>DTS<br/></sub>DTG[7:5] = 111 → DT = (32+DTG[4:0])xt<sub>dtg</sub> with T<sub>dtg</sub> = 16xt<sub>DTS<br/></sub>Example if T<sub>DTS</sub> = 125 ns (8MHz), dead-time possible values are:<br/>0 to 15875 ns by 125 ns steps,<br/>16 µs to 31750 ns by 250 ns steps,<br/>32 µs to 63 µs by 1 µs steps,<br/>64 µs to 126 µs by 2 µs steps</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bitfield can not be modified as long as LOCK level 1, 2 or 3 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIM15_BDTR register).</p></td></tr></table></div>

style="font-weight:Bold;">DTPE</span>: Deadtime preload enable</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Deadtime value is not preloaded</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Deadtime value preload is enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit can not be modified as long as LOCK level 1, 2 or 3 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIM15_BDTR register).</p></td></tr><tr height="102.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DTAE</span>: Deadtime asymmetric enable</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   Deadtime on rising and falling edges are identical, and defined with DTG[7:0] register</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   Deadtime on rising edge is defined with DTG[7:0] register and deadtime on falling edge is defined with DTGF[7:0] bits.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit can not be modified as long as LOCK level 1, 2 or 3 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIM15_BDTR register).</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="220.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 7:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DTGF[7:0]</span>: Dead-time falling edge generator setup</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the duration of the dead-time inserted between the complementary outputs, on the falling edge.</p><p class="TableIndent">DTGF[7:5] = 0xx → DTF = DTGF[7:0]x t<sub>dtg</sub> with t<sub>dtg</sub> = t<sub>DTS</sub>.<br/>DTGF[7:5] = 10x → DTF = (64+DTGF[5:0])xt<sub>dtg</sub> with T<sub>dtg</sub> = 2xt<sub>DTS</sub>.<br/>DTGF[7:5] = 110 → DTF = (32+DTGF[4:0])xt<sub>dtg</sub> with T<sub>dtg</sub> = 8xt<sub>DTS</sub>.<br/>DTGF[7:5] = 111 → DTF = (32+DTGF[4:0])xt<sub>dtg</sub> with T<sub>dtg</sub> = 16xt<sub>DTS</sub>.<br/>Example if T<sub>DTS</sub> = 125 ns (8 MHz), dead-time possible values are:<br/>0 to 15875 ns by 125 ns steps,<br/>16 μs to 31750 ns by 250 ns steps,<br/>32 μs to 63 μs by 1 μs steps,<br/>64 μs to 126 μs by 2 μs steps</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bitfield can not be modified as long as LOCK level 1, 2 or 3 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIM15_BDTR register).</p></td></tr></table></div>

<div align="left" data-conditional="_gpt2lcv4_tim2cc"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="114.23px"/><col width="497.75px"/><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DMAB[31:0]</span>: DMA register for burst accesses</p><p class="TableIndent">A read or write operation to the DMAR register accesses the register located at the address</p><p class="TableBodyC">(TIM15_CR1 address) + (DBA + DMA index) x 4 </p><p class="TableIndent">where TIM15_CR1 address is the address of the control register 1, DBA is the DMA base address configured in TIM15_DCR register, DMA index is automatically controlled by the DMA transfer, and ranges from 0 to DBL (DBL configured in TIM15_DCR).</p></td></tr></table></div>

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="114.77px"/><col width="496.81px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:13</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="73.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 12</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DITHEN</span>: Dithering enable</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Dithering disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Dithering enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The DITHEN bit can only be modified when CEN bit is reset.</p></td></tr><tr height="54.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 11</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">UIFREMAP</span>: UIF status bit remapping</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No remapping. UIF status bit is not copied to TIMx_CNT register bit 31.<br/>1: Remapping enabled. UIF status bit is copied to TIMx_CNT register bit 31.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="129.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 9:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CKD[1:0]</span>: Clock division</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield indicates the division ratio between the timer clock (tim_ker_ck) frequency and the dead-time and sampling clock (t<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">DTS</span></sub>)used by the dead-time generators and the digital filters (tim_tix),</p><p class="TableIndent">00: t<sub>DTS</sub> = t<sub>tim_ker_ck<br/></sub>01: t<sub>DTS</sub> = 2*t<sub>tim_ker_ck<br/></sub>10: t<sub>DTS</sub> = 4*t<sub>tim_ker_ck<br/></sub>11: Reserved</p></td></tr><tr height="54.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ARPE</span>: Auto-reload preload enable</p><p class="TableIndent">0: TIMx_ARR register is not buffered<br/>1: TIMx_ARR register is buffered</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 6:4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="54.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OPM</span>: One pulse mode</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Counter is not stopped at update event<br/>1: Counter stops counting at the next update event (clearing the bit CEN)</p></td></tr><tr height="138.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">URS</span>:<span style="font-weight:Bold;"> </span>Update request source</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software to select the UEV event sources.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   Any of the following events generate an update interrupt or DMA request if enabled. These events can be: </p><p class="RegTBullet2">–<span style="padding-right:16pt ;">​</span>Counter overflow/underflow</p><p class="RegTBullet2">–<span style="padding-right:16pt ;">​</span>Setting the UG bit</p><p class="RegTBullet2">–<span style="padding-right:16pt ;">​</span>Update generation through the slave mode controller</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:    nly counter overflow/underflow generates an update interrupt or DMA request if enabled.</p></td></tr><tr height="169.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">UDIS</span>:<span style="font-style:Italic;"> </span>Update disable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software to enable/disable UEV event generation.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   UEV enabled. The Update (UEV) event is generated by one of the following events:</p><p class="RegTBullet2">–<span style="padding-right:16pt ;">​</span>Counter overflow/underflow</p><p class="RegTBullet2">–<span style="padding-right:16pt ;">​</span>Setting the UG bit</p><p class="RegTBullet2">–<span style="padding-right:16pt ;">​</span>Update generation through the slave mode controller</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">   Buffered registers are then loaded with their preload values.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   UEV disabled. The Update event is not generated, shadow registers keep their value (ARR, PSC, CCRx). However the counter and the prescaler are reinitialized if the UG bit is set or if a hardware reset is received from the slave mode controller.</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CEN</span>: Counter enable</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Counter disabled<br/>1: Counter enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>External clock and gated mode can work only if the CEN bit has been previously set by software. However trigger mode can set the CEN bit automatically by hardware.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 31.8.2 TIMx control register 2 (TIMx\_CR2)(x = 16 to 17)

8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OIS1</span>: Output Idle state 1 (tim_oc1 output)</p><p class="TableIndent">0: tim_oc1 = 0 after a dead-time when MOE = 0<br/>1: tim_oc1 = 1 after a dead-time when MOE = 0</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit can not be modified as long as LOCK level 1, 2 or 3 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIMx_BKR register).</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 7:4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="54.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CCDS</span>: Capture/compare DMA selection</p><p class="TableIndent">0: CCx DMA request sent when CCx event occurs<br/>1: CCx DMA requests sent when update event occurs</p></td></tr><tr height="102.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CCUS</span>:<span style="font-style:Italic;"> </span>Capture/compare control update selection</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:    When capture/compare control bits are preloaded (CCPC = 1), they are updated by setting the COMG bit only.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   When capture/compare control bits are preloaded (CCPC = 1), they are updated by setting the COMG bit or when a rising edge occurs on tim_trgi (if available).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit acts only on channels that have a complementary output.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   CCxE, CCxNE and OCxM bits are not preloaded</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   CCxE, CCxNE and OCxM bits are preloaded, after having been written, they are updated only when COM bit is set.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit acts only on channels that have a complementary output.</p></td></tr></table></div>

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="114.50px"/><col width="495.27px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="101.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 9</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC1OF</span>: Capture/Compare 1 overcapture flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This flag is set by hardware only when the corresponding channel is configured in input capture mode. It is cleared by software by writing it to 0.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   No overcapture has been detected</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   The counter value has been captured in TIMx_CCR1 register while CC1IF flag was already set</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="84.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BIF</span>: Break interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This flag is set by hardware as soon as the tim_brk input goes active. It can be cleared by software if the break input is not active.<br/>0: No break event occurred<br/>1: An active level has been detected on the break input</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 6</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="85.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="Bold" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:Bold;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">COMIF:</span> COM interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This flag is set by hardware on a COM event (once the capture/compare control bits –CCxE, CCxNE, OCxM– have been updated). It is cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No COM event occurred<br/>1: COM interrupt pending</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 4:2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="221.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC1IF</span>: Capture/Compare 1 interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This flag is set by hardware. It is cleared by software (input capture or output compare mode) or by reading the TIMx_CCR1 register (input capture mode only).</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No compare match / No input capture occurred</p><p class="TableIndent">1: A compare match or an input capture occurred</p><p class="TableIndent"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC1 is configured as output</span>: this flag is set when the content of the counter TIMx_CNT matches the content of the TIMx_CCR1 register. When the content of TIMx_CCR1 is greater than the content of TIMx_ARR, the CC1IF bit goes high on the counter overflow (in up-counting and up/down-counting modes) or underflow (in down-counting mode). There are 3 possible options for flag setting in center-aligned mode, refer to the CMS bits in the TIMx_CR1 register for the full description.</p><p class="TableIndent"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC1 is configured as input</span>: this bit is set when counter value has been captured in TIMx_CCR1 register (an edge has been detected on IC1, as per the edge sensitivity defined with the CC1P and CC1NP bits setting, in TIMx_CCER).</p></td></tr><tr height="133.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">UIF</span>: Update interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware on an update event. It is cleared by software.<br/>0: No update occurred.<br/>1: Update interrupt pending. This bit is set by hardware when the registers are updated:</p><p class="RegTBullet2">–<span style="padding-right:16pt ;">​</span>At overflow regarding the repetition counter value (update if repetition counter = 0) and if the UDIS = 0 in the TIMx_CR1 register.</p><p class="RegTBullet2">–<span style="padding-right:16pt ;">​</span>When CNT is reinitialized by software using the UG bit in TIMx_EGR register, if URS = 0 and UDIS = 0 in the TIMx_CR1 register.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 31.8.5 TIMx event generation register (TIMx\_EGR)(x = 16 to 17)

Address offset: 0x14

Reset value: 0x0000
