<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="113.79px"/><col width="497.21px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="101.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BG</span>: Break generation</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by software in order to generate an event, it is automatically cleared by hardware.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   No action.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   A break event is generated. MOE bit is cleared and BIF flag is set. Related interrupt or DMA transfer can occur if enabled.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 6</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="88.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="Bold" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:Bold;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">COMG:</span> Capture/Compare control update generation</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit can be set by software, it is automatically cleared by hardware.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No action<br/>1: When the CCPC bit is set, it is possible to update the CCxE, CCxNE and OCxM bits</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit acts only on channels that have a complementary output.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 4:2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="172.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC1G</span>: Capture/Compare 1 generation</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by software in order to generate an event, it is automatically cleared by hardware.<br/>0: No action.<br/>1: A capture/compare event is generated on channel 1:<br/><span style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC1 is configured as output:<br/></span>CC1IF flag is set, Corresponding interrupt or DMA request is sent if enabled.<br/><span style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC1 is configured as input:<br/></span>The current value of the counter is captured in TIMx_CCR1 register. The CC1IF flag is set, the corresponding interrupt or DMA request is sent if enabled. The CC1OF flag is set if the CC1IF flag was already high.</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">UG</span>: Update generation</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">This bit can be set by software, it is automatically cleared by hardware.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   No action.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   Reinitialize the counter and generates an update of the registers. Note that the prescaler counter is cleared too (anyway the prescaler ratio is not affected). </p></td></tr></table></div>


### 31.8.6 TIMx capture/compare mode register 1 (TIMx\_CCMR1)  
   (x = 16 to 17)

Address offset: 0x18

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

The same register can be used for input capture mode (this section) or for output compare mode (next section). The direction of a channel is defined by configuring the corresponding CCxS bits. All the other bits of this register have a different function for input capture and for output compare modes. It is possible to combine both modes independently (for example channel 1 in input capture mode and channel 2 in output compare mode).

font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/32, N = 8</p></td></tr><tr height="113.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 3:2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IC1PSC[1:0]</span>:<span style="font-style:Italic;"> </span>Input capture 1 prescaler</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the ratio of the prescaler acting on CC1 input (tim_ic1).<br/>The prescaler is reset as soon as CC1E = 0 (TIMx_CCER register).<br/>00: no prescaler, capture is done each time an edge is detected on the capture input.<br/>01: capture is done once every 2 events<br/>10: capture is done once every 4 events<br/>11: capture is done once every 8 events</p></td></tr><tr height="105.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 1:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC1S[1:0]</span>: Capture/Compare 1 selection</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the direction of the channel (input/output) as well as the used input.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">00:   CC1 channel is configured as output</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">01:   CC1 channel is configured as input, tim_ic1 is mapped on tim_ti1</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">Others: Reserved</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>CC1S bits are writable only when the channel is OFF (CC1E = 0 in TIMx_CCER).</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 31.8.7   
TIMx capture/compare mode register 1 [alternate]   (TIMx\_CCMR1)(x = 16 to 17)

Address offset: 0x18

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

The same register can be used for output compare mode (this section) or for input capture mode (previous section). The direction of a channel is defined by configuring the corresponding CCxS bits. All the other bits of this register have a different function for input capture and for output compare modes. It is possible to combine both modes independently (for example channel 1 in input capture mode and channel 2 in output compare mode).

Output compare mode:

 


<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.41px"/><col width="493.03px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:17</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="54.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC1CE</span>: Output Compare 1 clear enable</p><p class="TableIndent">0: tim_oc1ref is not affected by the tim_ocref_clr input.<br/>1: tim_oc1ref is cleared as soon as a High level is detected on tim_ocref_clr input.</p></td></tr><tr height="394.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 16, 6:4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC1M[3:0]</span>: Output Compare 1 mode</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits define the behavior of the output reference signal tim_oc1ref from which tim_oc1 and tim_oc1n are derived. tim_oc1ref is active high whereas tim_oc1 and tim_oc1n active level depends on CC1P and CC1NP bits.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0000:   Frozen - The comparison between the output compare register TIMx_CCR1 and the counter TIMx_CNT has no effect on the outputs. This mode can be used when the timer serves as a software timebase. When the frozen mode is enabled during timer operation, the output keeps the state (active or inactive) it had before entering the frozen state.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0001:   Set channel 1 to active level on match. tim_oc1ref signal is forced high when the counter TIMx_CNT matches the capture/compare register 1 (TIMx_CCR1).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0010:   Set channel 1 to inactive level on match. tim_oc1ref signal is forced low when the counter TIMx_CNT matches the capture/compare register 1 (TIMx_CCR1).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0011:   Toggle - tim_oc1ref toggles when TIMx_CNT = TIMx_CCR1.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0100:   Force inactive level - tim_oc1ref is forced low.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0101:   Force active level - tim_oc1ref is forced high.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0110:   PWM mode 1 - Channel 1 is active as long as TIMx_CNT&lt;TIMx_CCR1 else inactive.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0111:   PWM mode 2 - Channel 1 is inactive as long as TIMx_CNT&lt;TIMx_CCR1 else active. </p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">Others: Reserved</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>These bits can not be modified as long as LOCK level 3 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIMx_BDTR register) and CC1S = 00 (the channel is configured in output).</p><p class="RegTNote_">In PWM mode, the OCREF level changes when the result of the comparison changes, when the output compare mode switches from “frozen” mode to “PWM” mode and when the output compare mode switches from “force active/inactive” mode to “PWM” mode.</p></td></tr><tr height="117.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC1PE</span>: Output Compare 1 preload enable</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   Preload register on TIMx_CCR1 disabled. TIMx_CCR1 can be written at anytime, the new value is taken in account immediately.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   Preload register on TIMx_CCR1 enabled. Read/Write operations access the preload register. TIMx_CCR1 preload value is loaded in the active register at each update event.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>These bits can not be modified as long as LOCK level 3 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIMx_BDTR register) and CC1S = 00 (the channel is configured in output).</p></td></tr><tr height="174.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC1FE</span>: Output Compare 1 fast enable</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">This bit decreases the latency between a trigger event and a transition on the timer output. It must be used in one-pulse mode (OPM bit set in TIMx_CR1 register), to have the output pulse starting as soon as possible after the starting trigger.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   CC1 behaves normally depending on counter and CCR1 values even when the trigger is ON. The minimum delay to activate CC1 output when an edge occurs on the trigger input is 5 clock cycles.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   An active edge on the trigger input acts like a compare match on CC1 output. Then, tim_ocx is set to the compare level independently of the result of the comparison. Delay to sample the trigger input and to activate CC1 output is reduced to 3 clock cycles. OC1FE acts only if the channel is configured in PWM1 or PWM2 mode.</p></td></tr><tr height="105.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 1:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC1S[1:0]</span>: Capture/Compare 1 selection</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the direction of the channel (input/output) as well as the used input.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">00: CC1 channel is configured as output</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">01: CC1 channel is configured as input, tim_ic1 is mapped on tim_ti1</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">Others: Reserved</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>CC1S bits are writable only when the channel is OFF (CC1E = 0 in TIMx_CCER).</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 31.8.8 TIMx capture/compare enable register (TIMx\_CCER)(x = 16 to 17)

Address offset: 0x20

Reset value: 0x0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.50px"/><col width="496.90px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="200.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC1NP</span>: Capture/Compare 1 complementary output polarity</p><p class="TableBodyL">CC1 channel configured as output:</p><p class="TableIndent">0: tim_oc1n active high<br/>1: tim_oc1n active low</p><p class="TableBodyL">CC1 channel configured as input:</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is used in conjunction with CC1P to define the polarity of tim_ti1fp1. Refer to the description of CC1P.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit is not writable as soon as LOCK level 2 or 3 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIMx_BDTR register) and CC1S = 00 (the channel is configured in output).</p><p class="RegTNote_">On channels that have a complementary output, this bit is preloaded. If the CCPC bit is set in the TIMx_CR2 register then the CC1NP active bit takes the new value from the preloaded bit only when a commutation event is generated.</p></td></tr><tr height="85.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC1NE</span>: Capture/Compare 1 complementary output enable</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   Off - tim_oc1n is not active. tim_oc1n level is then function of MOE, OSSI, OSSR, OIS1, OIS1N and CC1E bits.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   On - tim_oc1n signal is output on the corresponding output pin depending on MOE, OSSI, OSSR, OIS1, OIS1N and CC1E bits.</p></td></tr><tr height="332.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC1P</span>: Capture/Compare 1 output polarity</p><p class="TableIndent">0: OC1 active high (output mode) / Edge sensitivity selection (input mode, see below)</p><p class="TableIndent">1: OC1 active low (output mode) / Edge sensitivity selection (input mode, see below)</p><p class="TableIndent"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">When CC1 channel is configured as input</span>, both CC1NP/CC1P bits select the active polarity of TI1FP1 and TI2FP1 for trigger or capture operations.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 104.88pt;">CC1NP = 0, CC1P = 0:   non-inverted/rising edge. The circuit is sensitive to TIxFP1 rising edge (capture or trigger operations in reset, external clock or trigger mode), TIxFP1 is not inverted (trigger operation in gated mode).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 104.88pt;">CC1NP = 0, CC1P = 1:   inverted/falling edge. The circuit is sensitive to TIxFP1 falling edge (capture or trigger operations in reset, external clock or trigger mode), TIxFP1 is inverted (trigger operation in gated mode).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 104.88pt;">CC1NP = 1, CC1P = 1:   non-inverted/both edges/ The circuit is sensitive to both TIxFP1 rising and falling edges (capture or trigger operations in reset, external clock or trigger mode), TIxFP1is not inverted (trigger operation in gated mode).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 104.88pt;">CC1NP = 1, CC1P = 0:   this configuration is reserved, it must not be used.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit is not writable as soon as LOCK level 2 or 3 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIMx_BDTR register).</p><p class="RegTNote_">On channels that have a complementary output, this bit is preloaded. If the CCPC bit is set in the TIMx_CR2 register then the CC1P active bit takes the new value from the preloaded bit only when a Commutation event is generated.</p></td></tr><tr height="101.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC1E</span>: Capture/Compare 1 output enable</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Capture mode disabled / OC1 is not active (see below)</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Capture mode enabled / OC1 signal is output on the corresponding output pin</p><p class="TableIndent"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">When CC1 channel is configured as output</span>, the OC1 level depends on MOE, OSSI, OSSR, OIS1, OIS1N and CC1NE bits, regardless of the CC1E bits state. Refer to <span class="CrossRef" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;"><a href="#XREF_88070__Table_168__Output_control_bits_for_complementary_OCx_and_OCxN22" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Table 318</a></span> for details.</p></td></tr></table></div>

**Note:**

The state of the external I/O pins connected to the complementary tim\_oc1 and tim\_oc1n channels depends on the tim\_oc1 and tim\_oc1n channel state and GPIO control and alternate function selection registers.

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

The ARR[19:16] bits are reset.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Dithering mode (DITHEN = 1)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the integer part in ARR[19:4]. <div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.14px"/><col width="496.84px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="194.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 7:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">REP[7:0]</span>: Repetition counter reload value</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the update rate of the compare registers (i.e. periodic transfers from preload to active registers) when preload registers are enable. It also defines the update interrupt generation rate, if this interrupt is enable.</p><p class="TableIndent">When the repetition down-counter reaches zero, an update event is generated and it restarts counting from REP value. As the repetition counter is reloaded with REP value only at the repetition update event UEV, any write to the TIMx_RCR register is not taken in account until the next repetition update event.</p><p class="TableIndent">It means in PWM mode (REP+1) corresponds to the number of PWM periods in edge-aligned mode:</p><p class="RegTBullet2">–<span style="padding-right:16pt ;">​</span>The number of PWM periods in edge-aligned mode.</p><p class="RegTBullet2">–<span style="padding-right:16pt ;">​</span>The number of half PWM period in center-aligned mode.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 31.8.13 TIMx capture/compare register 1 (TIMx\_CCR1)(x = 16 to 17)

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.14px"/><col width="495.93px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:20</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="304.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 19:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CCR1[19:0]</span>: Capture/Compare 1 value</p><p class="TableIndent"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC1 is configured as output</span>:<br/>CCR1 is the value to be loaded in the actual capture/compare 1 register (preload value).</p><p class="TableIndent">It is loaded permanently if the preload feature is not selected in the TIMx_CCMR1 register (bit OC1PE). Else the preload value is copied in the active capture/compare 1 register when an update event occurs.</p><p class="TableIndent">The active capture/compare register contains the value to be compared to the counter TIMx_CNT and signaled on tim_oc1 output.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Non-dithering mode (DITHEN = 0)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the compare value in CCR1[15:0]. The CCR1[19:16] bits are reset.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Dithering mode (DITHEN = 1)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the integer part in CCR1[19:4]. The CCR1[3:0] bitfield contains the dithered part.</p><p class="TableIndent"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC1 is configured as input</span>:<br/>CCR1 is the counter value transferred by the last input capture 1 event (tim_ic1).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Non-dithering mode (DITHEN = 0)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the capture value in CCR1[15:0]. The CCR1[19:16] bits are reset.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Dithering mode (DITHEN = 1)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the capture in CCR1[19:4]. The CCR1[3:0] bits are reset.</p></td></tr></table></div>

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

**Note:**

As the BKBID, BKDSRM, BKF[3:0], AOE, BKP, BKE, OSSI, OSSR, and DTG[7:0] bits may be write-locked depending on the LOCK configuration, it may be necessary to configure all of them during the first write access to the TIMx\_BDTR register.

 


<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="113.32px"/><col width="499.69px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:29</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="149.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 28</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BKBID</span>: Break Bidirectional</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Break input tim_brk in input mode<br/>1: Break input tim_brk in bidirectional mode</p><p class="TableIndent">In the bidirectional mode (BKBID bit set to 1), the break input is configured both in input mode and in open drain output mode. Any active break event asserts a low logic level on the Break input to indicate an internal break event to external devices.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit cannot be modified as long as LOCK level 1 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIMx_BDTR register).</p><p class="RegTNote_">Any write operation to this bit takes a delay of 1 APB clock cycle to become effective.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 27</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="133.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 26</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BKDSRM</span>: Break Disarm</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Break input tim_brk is armed<br/>1: Break input tim_brk is disarmed</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is cleared by hardware when no break source is active.</p><p class="TableIndent">The BKDSRM bit must be set by software to release the bidirectional output control (open-drain output in Hi-Z state) and then be polled it until it is reset by hardware, indicating that the fault condition has disappeared.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>Any write operation to this bit takes a delay of 1 APB clock cycle to become effective.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 25:20</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="336.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 19:16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BKF[3:0]</span>:<span style="font-weight:Bold;"> </span>Break filter</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the frequency used to sample tim_brk input and the length of the digital filter applied to tim_brk. The digital filter is made of an event counter in which N events are needed to validate a transition on the output:</p><p class="TableIndent">0000: No filter, tim_brk acts asynchronously<br/>0001: f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>tim_ker_ck</sub>, N = 2<br/>0010: f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>tim_ker_ck</sub>, N = 4<br/>0011: f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>tim_ker_ck</sub>, N = 8<br/>0100: f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/2, N = 6<br/>0101: f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/2, N = 8<br/>0110: f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/4, N = 6<br/>0111: f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/4, N = 8<br/>1000: f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/8, N = 6<br/>1001: f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/8, N = 8<br/>1010: f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/16, N = 5<br/>1011: f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/16, N = 6<br/>1100: f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/16, N = 8<br/>1101: f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/32, N = 5<br/>1110: f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/32, N = 6<br/>1111: f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/32, N = 8</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit cannot be modified when LOCK level 1 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIMx_BDTR register).</p></td></tr><tr height="161.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 15</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">MOE</span>: Main output enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is cleared asynchronously by hardware as soon as the tim_brk input is active. It is set by software or automatically depending on the AOE bit. It is acting only on the channels which are configured in output.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   tim_oc1 and tim_oc1n outputs are disabled or forced to idle state depending on the OSSI bit.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   tim_oc1 and tim_oc1n outputs are enabled if their respective enable bits are set (CC1E, CC1NE in TIMx_CCER register)</p><p class="TableIndent">See tim_oc1/tim_oc1n enable description for more details (<span class="CrossRef" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;"><a href="#XREF_84854__41_7_7_TIM16/TIM17_capture/compare_enable_register_(TIMx_CCER)22" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 31.8.8: TIMx capture/compare enable register (TIMx_CCER)(x = 16 to 17)</a></span>).</p></td></tr><tr height="102.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 14</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">AOE</span>: Automatic output enable</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   MOE can be set only by software</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   MOE can be set by software or automatically at the next update event (if the tim_brk input is not active)</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit can not be modified as long as LOCK level 1 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIMx_BDTR register).</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 13</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BKP</span>: Break polarity</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Break input tim_brk is active low<br/>1: Break input tim_brk is active high</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit can not be modified as long as LOCK level 1 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIMx_BDTR register).</p><p class="RegTNote_">Any write operation to this bit takes a delay of 1 APB clock cycle to become effective.</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 12</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BKE</span>: Break enable</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Break inputs (tim_brk and tim_sys_brk event) disabled<br/>1; Break inputs (tim_brk and tim_sys_brk event) enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit cannot be modified when LOCK level 1 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIMx_BDTR register).</p><p class="RegTNote_">Any write operation to this bit takes a delay of 1 APB clock cycle to become effective.</p></td></tr><tr height="192.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 11</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OSSR</span>:<span style="font-weight:Bold;"> </span>Off-state selection for Run mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is used when MOE = 1 on channels that have a complementary output which are configured as outputs. OSSR is not implemented if no complementary output is implemented in the timer.<br/>See tim_oc1/tim_oc1n enable description for more details (<span class="CrossRef" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;"><a href="#XREF_84854__41_7_7_TIM16/TIM17_capture/compare_enable_register_(TIMx_CCER)22" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 31.8.8: TIMx capture/compare enable register (TIMx_CCER)(x = 16 to 17)</a></span>).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   When inactive, tim_oc1/tim_oc1n outputs are disabled (the timer releases the output control which is taken over by the GPIO, which forces a Hi-Z state)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   When inactive, tim_oc1/tim_oc1n outputs are enabled with their inactive level as soon as CC1E = 1 or CC1NE = 1 (the output is still controlled by the timer).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit can not be modified as soon as the LOCK level 2 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIMx_BDTR register).</p></td></tr><tr height="162.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OSSI</span>:<span style="font-weight:Bold;"> </span>Off-state selection for Idle mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is used when MOE = 0 on channels configured as outputs.<br/>See tim_oc1/tim_oc1n enable description for more details (<span class="CrossRef" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;"><a href="#XREF_84854__41_7_7_TIM16/TIM17_capture/compare_enable_register_(TIMx_CCER)22" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 31.8.8: TIMx capture/compare enable register (TIMx_CCER)(x = 16 to 17)</a></span>).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   When inactive, tim_oc1/tim_oc1n outputs are disabled (tim_oc1/tim_oc1n enable output signal = 0)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   When inactive, tim_oc1/tim_oc1n outputs are forced first with their idle level as soon as CC1E = 1 or CC1NE = 1. tim_oc1/tim_oc1n enable output signal = 1)</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit can not be modified as soon as the LOCK level 2 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIMx_BDTR register).</p></td></tr><tr height="209.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 9:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">LOCK[1:0]</span>: Lock configuration</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits offer a write protection against software errors.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">00:   LOCK OFF - No bit is write protected</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">01:   LOCK Level 1 = DTG bits in TIMx_BDTR register, OISx and OISxN bits in TIMx_CR2 register and BKBID/BKE/BKP/AOE bits in TIMx_BDTR register can no longer be written.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">10:   LOCK Level 2 = LOCK Level 1 + CC Polarity bits (CCxP/CCxNP bits in TIMx_CCER register, as long as the related channel is configured in output through the CCxS bits) as well as OSSR and OSSI bits can no longer be written.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 25.51pt;">11:   LOCK Level 3 = LOCK Level 2 + CC Control bits (OCxM and OCxPE bits in TIMx_CCMRx registers, as long as the related channel is configured in output through the CCxS bits) can no longer be written.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The LOCK bits can be written only once after the reset. Once the TIMx_BDTR register has been written, their content is frozen until the next reset.</p></td></tr><tr height="218.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 7:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DTG[7:0]</span>: Dead-time generator setup</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the duration of the dead-time inserted between the complementary outputs. DT correspond to this duration.<br/>DTG[7:5] = 0xx → DT = DTG[7:0]x t<sub>dtg</sub> with t<sub>dtg</sub> = t<sub>DTS<br/></sub>DTG[7:5] = 10x → DT = (64+DTG[5:0])xt<sub>dtg</sub> with T<sub>dtg</sub> = 2xt<sub>DTS<br/></sub>DTG[7:5] = 110 → DT = (32+DTG[4:0])xt<sub>dtg</sub> with T<sub>dtg</sub> = 8xt<sub>DTS<br/></sub>DTG[7:5] = 111 → DT = (32+DTG[4:0])xt<sub>dtg</sub> with T<sub>dtg</sub> = 16xt<sub>DTS<br/></sub>Example if T<sub>DTS</sub>=125 ns (8 MHz), dead-time possible values are:<br/>0 to 15875 ns by 125 ns steps,<br/>16 µs to 31750 ns by 250 ns steps,<br/>32 µs to 63 µs by 1 µs steps,<br/>64 µs to 126 µs by 2 µs steps</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bitfield can not be modified as long as LOCK level 1, 2 or 3 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIMx_BDTR register).</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 31.8.15 TIMx timer deadtime register 2 (TIMx\_DTR2)(x = 16 to 17)

Address offset: 0x054

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.72px"/><col width="498.45px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:18</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="88.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 17</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DTPE</span>: Deadtime preload enable</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Deadtime value is not preloaded</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Deadtime value preload is enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit can not be modified as long as LOCK level 1, 2 or 3 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIMx_BDTR register).</p></td></tr><tr height="102.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DTAE</span>: Deadtime asymmetric enable</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   Deadtime on rising and falling edges are identical, and defined with DTG[7:0] register</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   Deadtime on rising edge is defined with DTG[7:0] register and deadtime on falling edge is defined with DTGF[7:0] bits.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit can not be modified as long as LOCK level 1, 2 or 3 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIMx_BDTR register).</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="220.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 7:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DTGF[7:0]</span>: Dead-time falling edge generator setup</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the duration of the dead-time inserted between the complementary outputs, on the falling edge.</p><p class="TableIndent">DTGF[7:5] = 0xx → DTF = DTGF[7:0]x t<sub>dtg</sub> with t<sub>dtg</sub> = t<sub>DTS</sub>.<br/>DTGF[7:5] = 10x → DTF = (64+DTGF[5:0])xt<sub>dtg</sub> with T<sub>dtg</sub> = 2xt<sub>DTS</sub>.<br/>DTGF[7:5] = 110 → DTF = (32+DTGF[4:0])xt<sub>dtg</sub> with T<sub>dtg</sub> = 8xt<sub>DTS</sub>.<br/>DTGF[7:5] = 111 → DTF = (32+DTGF[4:0])xt<sub>dtg</sub> with T<sub>dtg</sub> = 16xt<sub>DTS</sub>.<br/>Example if T<sub>DTS</sub> = 125 ns (8 MHz), dead-time possible values are:<br/>0 to 15875 ns by 125 ns steps,<br/>16 μs to 31750 ns by 250 ns steps,<br/>32 μs to 63 μs by 1 μs steps,<br/>64 μs to 126 μs by 2 μs steps</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bitfield can not be modified as long as LOCK level 1, 2 or 3 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIMx_BDTR register).</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 31.8.16 TIMx input selection register (TIMx\_TISEL)(x = 16 to 17)

Address offset: 0x5C

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

style="display: none"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:13</p></td><td data-conditional="_gpt2lcv4_1,_gpt2lcv4_2,_gpt2lcv4_3,_gpt2lcv4_4,_gpt2lcv4_5" style="display: none"><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="144.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 12:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DBL[4:0]</span>: DMA burst length</p><p class="TableIndent">This 5-bitfield defines the length of DMA transfers (the timer recognizes a burst transfer when a read or a write access is done to the TIMx_DMAR address), i.e. the number of transfers. Transfers can be in half-words or in bytes (see example below).</p><p class="TableIndent">00000: 1 transfer,<br/>00001: 2 transfers,<br/>00010: 3 transfers,<br/>...<br/>10001: 18 transfers.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 7:5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="174.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 4:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DBA[4:0]</span>: DMA base address</p><p class="TableIndent">This 5-bitfield defines the base-address for DMA transfers (when read/write access are done through the TIMx_DMAR address). DBA is defined as an offset starting from the address of the TIMx_CR1 register.<br/>Example:<br/>00000: TIMx_CR1,<br/>00001: TIMx_CR2,<br/>00010: TIMx_SMCR,<br/>...</p><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="Bold" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:Bold;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Example:</span> Let us consider the following transfer: DBL = 7 transfers and DBA = TIMx_CR1. In this case the transfer is done to/from 7 registers starting from the TIMx_CR1 address.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 31.8.21 TIM16/TIM17 DMA address for full transfer  
   (TIMx\_DMAR)(x = 16 to 17)

Address offset: 0x3E0

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="114.23px"/><col width="497.75px"/><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DMAB[31:0]</span>: DMA register for burst accesses</p><p class="TableIndent">A read or write operation to the DMAR register accesses the register located at the address</p><p class="TableBodyC">(TIMx_CR1 address) + (DBA + DMA index) x 4 </p><p class="TableIndent">where TIMx_CR1 address is the address of the control register 1, DBA is the DMA base address configured in TIMx_DCR register, DMA index is automatically controlled by the DMA transfer, and ranges from 0 to DBL (DBL configured in TIMx_DCR).</p></td></tr></table></div>
